<p>“Hunter Yoon Seong-hyeon, please come with us. We’ll explain everything once we get there.”</p><p>“Huh?”</p><p>After finishing breakfast, I was helping Yu-na organize side dishes to send to Echo tomorrow when Hunter Association employees showed up at the house.</p><p>They wore grave expressions as they urgently asked me to come with them to the Association.</p><p>It was sudden, but then Han Ji-hyeok called, saying it was an emergency and asking if I could come to the Association right away.</p><p>“Y-Yes… I’ll just tell my family and be right out.”</p><p>In the end, still in a hoodie, sweatpants, and dragging my slippers, I got into the Association staff’s car and headed to the building.</p><p>“Can you at least tell me what this is about?”</p><p>“Well… we originally came to handle paperwork for Hunter Yoon Seong-hyeon’s food delivery mission tomorrow, but another issue came up. I’m sorry, but I don’t have the authority to disclose it. My apologies.”</p><p>“It’s fine…”</p><p>The staff member in the passenger seat bowed his head to me in apology.</p><p>My mind started racing with possibilities.</p><p>‘What the hell? Did something get exposed?’</p><p>No. Even if my depraved, taboo-breaking private life got out, they wouldn’t overreact this much.</p><p>Judging by their expressions, it had to be serious.</p><p>‘Did another S-rank Gate appear? Did a monster like Echo show up, one that’s hostile to humans?’</p><p>I cycled through every possibility, but none of them felt right.</p><p>“This way, please.”</p><p>When we arrived at the Association, the staff waiting at the main entrance of the central headquarters guided me inside. Among a sea of people in suits, I was the only one dressed like a bum, surrounded by six escorts. The forums generally had a very negative view of the Association, so whenever someone posted something overly positive or praiseworthy about them, the comments would flood with things like *‘Arrested in the Intelligence Bureau’s basement’* or *‘The Intelligence Bureau’s hiring comment shills these days, huh?’* But I never thought it actually existed.</p><p>‘But why are they taking me there?’</p><p>If they wanted to interrogate me about something, they would’ve arrested me. There was no reason to escort me to the basement this politely.</p><p>“Haa…”</p><p>As I sighed, the burly Hunter Association member turned his head toward me and said,</p><p>“You can rest assured, Hunter-nim. Nothing harmful will happen to you.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>The elevator stopped without the usual arrival chime, instead letting out a creaky, eerie *kiiik* as the doors opened.</p><p>The underground interrogation room I was seeing for the first time radiated a damp, oppressive energy. Han Ji-hyeok dismissed the other Association members, then led me away to a secluded spot.</p><p>The place we arrived at with Han Ji-hyeok had two Association members in suits, and in front of them was a glass window showing the inside of an interrogation room.</p><p>Inside that room, a terrified-looking man sat across from an Association member.</p><p>“Association President-nim, what’s going on here?”</p><p>The scene before me was like something out of a movie: through the one-way glass, an Association member in a rolled-up dress shirt slammed a file onto the table, shouting at the trembling man.</p><p>When the Association President nodded to the member beside him, the man turned to me and explained,</p><p>“This morning, two Association members were heading to Hunter Yoon Seong-hyeon’s home to process some documents when they spotted a suspicious man lurking and observing the houses in this area. Our house?”</p><p>Even as we spoke, the man inside didn’t seem to notice us, so this glass must’ve been designed so only we could see in. But no matter how I looked at him, the plump, frightened man was a complete stranger.</p><p>“I don’t know him.”</p><p>“We checked his identity too, but we couldn’t find any connection to you.
